hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $1$.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than $1$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**

!

[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 1. A line running to the right starts at 1 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < 1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 1. A line running to the right starts at negative 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6cb0017a77a27610e1b9255c8f26a339db58f50d)

The graph of $x >0$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 0. A line running to the right starts at 0 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/425c273291a50896db90fef4495d9a36bec3d02d)

The graph of $x <1$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 1. A line running to the left starts at 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3977545e176131825f917115c7d6f358e0b4266b)
